messages:
Alex: heads-up — competitor 'NimbusAI' announced a new routing feature that auto-falls back to cheaper models per request. saw notes from @sales. thoughts on response? :thinking:
Sam: saw the announcement. customers already pinging us. we should map responses to customer archetypes: startups (cost-first), enterprises (SLA/security), platform teams (controls). quick vote on parity vs differentiate per archetype?
Priya: engineering: full parity (match behaviour exactly) is expensive — we'd need model chaining + per-request routing + billing. recommend 3 response buckets: Parity mimic, Controls-first (enterprise), and Differentiator (policy marketplace).
Diego: ML note: we can prototype a lightweight policy router in 2 sprints leveraging current routing infra + cached metadata. main risk is fallback mismatch producing poor completions.
Maya: sales: ACME + a couple more pilots are explicitly asking for per-request routing and audit trails. they'd pay for dedicated if we ship enterprise-grade controls. parity for enterprise is high-priority from sales pipeline perspective.
Jin: design: we need a clear admin UX for policy creation + safe defaults. propose templates (cost-first, latency-first, quality-first). I can mock this next week.
Alex: propose mini-experiments (2-week windows for A/B, 4-week for C). draft launch criteria:
```
- Experiment A (Parity mimic): 2-week pilot, SLO: 99.5% uptime, tail latency <500ms for 90% of routed traffic, one paying pilot or documented customer intent
- Experiment B (Controls surface): 2-week pilot, expose per-tenant routing rules, audit logs + export, 2 enterprise trials committed
- Experiment C (Differentiator): 4-week build, policy marketplace + recommended quant profiles, KPI: demonstrable 10% cost reduction for representative prompt set
```
Priya: rough effort estimates: A = ~6 eng-weeks (spike + minimal integrations), B = ~4 eng-weeks (API + audit + UI), C = ~8 eng-weeks (policy infra + recommendations) + ML tuning. need prioritization guidance.
Sam: recommend we prioritize B (controls) because it unlocks enterprise deals. run A as a narrow spike behind a feature flag to gather feasibility data. C should be scoped after B proves demand.
Lydia: agree with prioritizing B. require a canary and auto-fallback plan: if routing causes a measurable quality regression, auto-fallback to baseline model and surface an incident ticket to the owning customer success rep.
Diego: monitoring checklist suggestion: embedding drift alert, perplexity / token-loss spike detection, latency histograms by policy, per-policy mismatch/error rate. we should tie alerts to per-pilot SLAs.
Alex: @Maya can you surface the top 3 accounts that care about per-request routing? we'll pick pilots from that list and prioritize outreach.
Maya: will DM the list by EOD. also need a pricing sketch: enterprise monthly premium vs metered per-request add-on.
Jin: will prototype the policy UX flows and a compact admin dashboard with CSV audit export + KMS tags for logs.
Priya: action owners (brief):
- Eng spike (A): owner @Diego
- B pilot infra + UX: owners @Priya + @Jin
- Pricing + sales pilot coordination: owner @Maya
- Success criteria & pilot playbook: owner @Sam
Alex: can we sync tomorrow 10:00am PT? 30m to land decisions and confirm owners. :calendar:
deploy-bot: Reminder: infra-alpha deploy scheduled for tomorrow 03:00 UTC — unrelated but flagging any potential infra work.
Sam: +1 for 10am. Alex, please drop experiment templates in the channel after the sync.
Alex: will post templates + short doc after meeting. thanks all :rocket:
